From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Northstar Payments — discovery recap & cost framing

Hi Alex / Jamie —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment and clear next steps. I captured the core pain, goals, and the earliest cost framing we discussed.

Key pain points (as described on the call):
- Fraud detection models are currently slowing page flow: long tail of requests causes occasional latency spikes (~800–1,200 ms) during peak.
- Token/compute unpredictability across different product flows (refunds vs checkout) → budgeting and unit economics are hard to forecast.
- Need to reduce inference cost while keeping accuracy (false-positive rate target: <1.2%).

Short-term goals (30–90 days):
- Run a 6–8 week pilot focused on the checkout fraud workflow (subset of traffic) to validate latency and cost savings.
- Demonstrate >=30% reduction in per-auth inference cost via batching + prefix/KV caching without degrading accuracy.
- Produce a decision memo for procurement with concrete TCO numbers and a recommended deployment (hosted vs dedicated).

Data points you shared on the call:
- Monthly volume (estimate): ~2.4M auths/month (average).
- Average tokens per request: ~450 input / ~120 output → ~570 tokens total.
- Peak concurrency: ~55 RPS, 5-minute bursts up to ~120 RPS.
- Current internal target budget: $25k–$35k/month for inference (pilot-friendly).

Initial token-econ sketch (very rough) — assumptions below:
- Baseline monthly tokens = 2.4M requests * 570 tokens ≈ 1.37B tokens/month.
- Redwood hosted nominal rate (assumption for sketch): $10 per 1M tokens (example SKU for generation-grade models).
- Baseline hosted spend ≈ $13.7k/month.
- With sensible batching + prefix/KV caching we typically see 30–45% token reduction on flows like yours; using 40% as midpoint -> effective tokens ≈ 822M -> est spend ≈ $8.2k/month.
- Dedicated/reserved can further reduce per-token costs but adds a fixed monthly commitment (example: 2x A100-equivalent pool + infra management ~ $5k/month). For your current volume the win depends on 12+ month commitment and expected growth.

What we need from you to firm up numbers (asks):
1) A sample of 200 representative payloads (sanitized) across the different auth types (checkout, refund, manual review) so we can run token distribution analysis.
2) Confirmation of the pilot traffic % (suggest 5–10% of auths to start).
3) Compliance checklist (SOC 2 / data residency constraints) so we can map to Private deployment requirements if needed.

Suggested next steps / timeline:
- Tessa/Jordan: prepare a one-page pilot proposal + line-item cost sketch (this week).
- Alex/Jamie: share sample payloads and confirm pilot % by EOD Wednesday (2026-10-07).
- Schedule a 60-minute working session (SE deep-dive) the week of Oct 12 to align on telemetry, rollout plan, and metrics.

Attachments: redwood-cost-playbook-v1.pdf (strawman), northstar-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

If any of the assumptions above are off, please flag and we'll correct the sketch. Happy to run sensitivity scenarios (e.g., 20% / 50% caching) once we have the payloads.

Best,

Thanks Tessa — really helpful summary. A few clarifications and quick answers to your asks:

- Budget: We have carved out $30k/month for pilot + scale experiments; that sits inside a larger fraud modernization budget.
- Payloads: We can share sanitized payloads — Jamie will export 250 examples from the last 6 weeks (will remove PII). Expect those by Tuesday EOD (2026-10-06).
- Pilot traffic: OK to start with 7% of checkout auths for the pilot.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II is a must; we also need data retention ≤30 days and key management options (KMS). Can you point to your SOC 2 report and KMS integrations?

On the token numbers — your 570 tokens/request is in the right range. A couple of follow-ups:
- Do you expect the batching savings % to be stable across both normal and burst traffic? Our concern is that burst windows (short-lived spikes) might not batch well, so we want conservative estimates for worst-case periods.
- When you say 'dedicated adds $5k/mo' — can you share a sample cost profile (reserved GPU + throughput SLA) so we can compare to hosted?

I've attached our signed NDA (NDA_signed.pdf). Once we get your SOC2 pointer and the Drive link for the pilot proposal, we'll confirm the internal procurement timeline (goal: decision within 8 weeks).

— Alex
Head of Fraud Engineering | Northstar Payments

Internal note (cc'ing Alex/Jamie for transparency) — quick technical sketch on where savings come from and what I'll prepare for the working session:

Assumptions we should validate from payloads: token distribution (P50/P90), sequence length variance per flow, and rate-profile (minute-level).

Opportunity map:
1) Batching: continuous batching at the runtime layer can smooth 20–35% of per-token compute inefficiency on steady traffic; on your median windows I expect ~30% savings, but during microbursts savings drop. We'll instrument spike-aware batching and set threshold windows so latency SLOs hold.

2) Prefix/KV caching: many auths share long common prefixes (merchant metadata + device signals). If we cache KV states at route-level we often see additional 10–25% token reduction for repeat patterns.

3) Model selection & quantization tradeoff: For fraud where hallucination risk is low, we can evaluate a quantized LLM variant for cost-per-token savings; typical accuracy impact is <1% for these tasks (we'll validate).

What I'll bring to the Oct 12 session:
- A sandbox runbook: step-by-step for sample payload ingestion and token profiling.
- Two pricing scenarios: Hosted (no commitment) with line-items; Dedicated (1-yr reserve) with amortized infra cost.
- Example latency profiles (tail latency with/without batching) from a similar customer.

Request to Alex/Jamie: please share the 250 examples and any available telemetry (p50/p95 token length) so I can pre-run the profiler. If you prefer, we can do a quick 30-min technical call next Tue (Oct 6) to align on telemetry schema.

— Jordan Blake
